觀測（because）：
Metal's shared and private buffer types BOTH return false from *_is_host(), so ggml_backend_buffer_is_host() prints 0 for every Metal buffer. A whole line of reasoning ('the table must be in a private buffer') rested on a field that cannot take another value.

它管轄的檔案：`src/llama.cpp/ggml/src/ggml-metal/ggml-metal-device.m`, `src/llama.cpp/src/llama-context.cpp`
A diagnostic field that is structurally constant carries no information: before reading a zero (or any fixed value) as evidence, find the code path that writes it and check it can vary at all.

換一個問題也適用，而且讀者手上沒有這筆 episode 也必須能照著做。

觀測（because）：
CGC_SLOT_TABLE_GPU builds the GPU table INSTEAD of the host remap leaf -- llama-graph.cpp:2178-2242 is an if/else, so for il >= CGC_S1_MIN_IL the leaf is never created and cache_remap_tensors[il] stays empty. The ONE increment of cache->n_zero_mapped_selected (llama-context.cpp:5475) sits inside the leaf-write block, which the hook skips when remap == nullptr. Every served layer therefore stops reporting the 'a selected expert read the ZERO slot' quality leak, and the teardown line (llama-expert-cache.cpp:2229) prints n_zero_mapped_selected=0 -- byte-identical to a run with no leak. The S1 A/B is documented as a pure scheduler/dispatch change; this monitoring change it carries silently is not in that description, and a gate that reads that counter would pass for the wrong reason. Note the code comment at llama-context.h:364 claims the opposite ('the leaf itself is still built when this is on'), which is how the trap survived review.

它實際被違反的紀錄（counterexample_observed）：
eng-20260915-210508-p25-slotgpu-l20-r1

它管轄的檔案：`src/llama.cpp/src/llama-graph.cpp`, `src/llama.cpp/src/llama-context.cpp`, `scripts/check/m123_oracle_gate.py`

When a change reroutes the code path that hosts a counter, that counter's zero is not evidence of absence: prove the instrument still runs on the layers being claimed before quoting any of its values.

以下是一條引擎調校迴圈裡「付過代價」的觀測。請把它一般化成**一條可重用的規訓**——
換一個問題也適用，而且讀者手上沒有這筆 episode 也必須能照著做。

觀測（because）：
The pool-row digest (a POOL row records the id a MoE consumer used and a digest of the bytes that id selected) was extended with the slot->expert map so the comparator could separate 'same slot, different expert' from 'same slot, same expert, different bytes'. The obvious implementation -- look the map up in the dump path, where the ids have just been read -- is wrong here for a reason particular to the investigation: the dump runs at synchronize, i.e. after the whole pass, so it would have read the map as it stood AFTER any background fill that landed late. 'A fill landed after the consumer had already read' is exactly the hypothesis the row was being used to test, so the label would have been produced by the phenomenon under test. The map itself does not depend on the ids, so it can be snapshotted at encode time (immediately before the consuming kernel is submitted) and stored per capture; the ids are consulted later, when they finally exist.

它實際被違反的紀錄（counterexample_observed）：
Instrument written 2026-09-17 (§9.18.7), not yet run. The contrast is measurable in the design itself: the same run's engine-side counter reports `consumed_changed=192` over one pass -- i.e. the consumed slot->expert map DOES move within a run -- while a hardcoded dump-time lookup would have shown one final value for every row and no way to see the movement at all.

它管轄的檔案：`src/llama.cpp/ggml/src/ggml-metal/ggml-metal-ops.cpp`, `src/llama.cpp/ggml/src/ggml-metal/ggml-metal-ops.h`

An annotation added to a reading must be sampled at the SAME instant as the reading, and if that instant is not the end of the step, the instrument must be built to run at the earlier one. Concretely: when a row records what a consumer SAW, anything that labels that row (which expert a slot holds, which owner a page belongs to, which generation a pointer came from) must be captured before or at the consumer, never at the synchronize point where the row is printed. The end-of-step state is a valid reading of its own -- but it is a different question, and it must not be used to label a within-step one, because the specific hypothesis such an instrument exists to test is usually 'did the thing that should have been in place before the read actually arrive before the read'.

QUESTION: The header comment on cache_slot_table_tensors says the leaf is still built under CGC_SLOT_TABLE_GPU and merely not consumed. Can that documented design be measured, i.e. is CGC_S1_BUILD_LEAF=1 a usable control?

EVIDENCE ON HAND:
- [artifact Backup/cgc_logs/llama_server_20260915_212420.log] p25-buildleaf never reached a single token: the server aborted at start with `ggml-alloc.c:623: GGML_ASSERT(buffer_id >= 0) failed`, stack ggml_gallocr_allocate_node <- ggml_gallocr_reserve_n_impl <- ggml_backend_sched_reserve <- llama_context::graph_reserve <- llama_context::sched_reserve <- llama_context::llama_context <- llama_init_from_model. The arm contributed no digest, so it says nothing about the logits.
- [artifact src/llama.cpp/src/llama-graph.cpp] In BUILD_LEAF the slots chain is neither consumed (remap_ids is left alone) nor expanded, so GET_ROWS/CONT/VIEW are orphaned and absent from cgraph->nodes; slot_table survives only because the ggml_build_forward_expand(gf, slot_table) above it is unconditional, and the newly constructed remap leaf is expanded too. Both are therefore graph ROOTS WITH NO CONSUMER, which is the configuration ggml-alloc rejects.
- [eng-20260915-212939-p25-slotgpu-dbg-r1] The contrast that makes the abort a finding rather than an accident: in the real arm the very same slot_table node is accepted (hook line: il=1 tbl=0x129c21650(tbl_data=0x12734c000), and the gather consumes it), and in the keep-leaf control the same node plus the leaf are accepted. Only 'present but consumed by nothing' fails.
    build=same-as-above  quotable=True

ALREADY RULED OUT (do not re-walk these):
- claim: The header comment on cache_slot_table_tensors describes what the S1 branch does, so CGC_S1_BUILD_LEAF=1 measures the intended design and a bit-identical result would licence 'follow the documentation' as the fix.
  why false: The arm does not run at all -- GGML_ASSERT(buffer_id >= 0) in ggml_gallocr_allocate_node, before any token is generated -- because a graph root with no consumer is never assigned a backend. A design that cannot be built cannot be measured.
- claim: The absence of the leaf node is a pure scheduler/dispatch change that leaves every other path bit-identical, as the comment asserts.
  why false: The comment's own premise is that the node is still built. Since it cannot be built unconsumed, the real arm's graph is genuinely different from every bit-identical reference -- one fewer pinned tensor, hence a different allocation -- so 'pure scheduler/dispatch change' is an assumption about the allocator that nothing has tested.

Retire the arm rather than re-add it: any future attempt to put the leaf back in the graph unconditionally needs an innocuous consumer, and there is no such consumer that does not change what mul_mat_id reads. The remaining structural suspect is the ggml-alloc layout change caused by removing a pinned node, and the instrument for that is GGML_SCHED_DEBUG=2's node-level backend/GET_CAUSE dump diffed between p25-gputime and p25-slotgpu, not another digest.

QUESTION: The whole-repo scan reports exactly 2 of 67 presence-tested knobs written as an explicit OFF-looking literal -- CGC_DBUF and CGC_SPAC in run_p1_mmap_stream.sh. Convert them to the same value-aware predicate? And what about CGC_DBUF2 / CGC_FAST_WAIT, which share the same non-empty spelling but are written nowhere; and what about the control-flow defect the same investigation exposed?

EVIDENCE ON HAND:
- [artifact src/llama.cpp/src/llama-expert-cache.h:521,532,543,573] The scan's classifier is too coarse for this family and had to be corrected before its answer could be acted on. It splits readers into 'presence-tested' vs 'value-parsed' by looking for `!= nullptr` in the line, so it labelled cgc_dbuf_on()/cgc_spac_on() as bare presence tests. They are not: their test is `getenv(...) != nullptr && getenv(...)[0] != '\0'`, a NON-EMPTY test. The behaviour is the same defect (a literal "0" is non-empty, hence ON) but the description and the fix differ, so the scan's label would have produced the wrong explanation even with the right knob names. Corrected family in llama-expert-cache.h: 4 helpers with the non-empty spelling -- cgc_dbuf_on (521), cgc_dbuf2_on (532), cgc_fast_wait_on (543), cgc_spac_on (573).
- [artifact scripts/run_p1_mmap_stream.sh:84-85, scripts/run_server.sh:1354] Only 2 of the 4 are written anywhere as a literal: run_p1_mmap_stream.sh:84-85 writes `CGC_DBUF=0` and `CGC_SPAC=0` directly into its SERVER_ENV, on the line beneath the comment saying P1 mode turns the pool optimisations off. CGC_DBUF2 and CGC_FAST_WAIT are assigned by no script, no python file and no doc. NOTE: run_server.sh DOES set CGC_DBUF after all (line 1354, `if [ "${CGC_DBUF:-1}" != "0" ]; then SERVER_ENV+=(CGC_DBUF=1); fi`). My first pass reported 'run_server.sh never sets them' -- a false negative from a grep whose pattern used `\|`, which BSD grep does not support, so it matched nothing. That false negative would have justified skipping this analysis entirely.
- [artifact Backup/cgc_logs/envdiff/pre_default.norm] The production launcher is already correct, and correct by a mechanism worth naming: run_server.sh only ever pushes `=1` and disables by pushing NOTHING. Measured with CGC_DUMP_ENV=1 on prefill250: default -> `ENV CGC_DBUF=1`; CGC_DBUF=0 -> CGC_DBUF absent from the env (off); CGC_SPAC=1 -> pushed; CGC_SPAC=0 -> absent. So the wrapper's documented 'set it to 0 to disable' worked by shell omission, not by the reader -- a literal `CGC_DBUF=0` pushed into SERVER_ENV would have meant ON. The comment at run_server.sh:1352-1353 was therefore true only by accident of how the emitting line was written.
- [artifact Backup/cgc_logs/envdiff/pre_default.norm vs post-fix fingerprint] Launch-env fingerprint, default prefill250, BEFORE the edits: md5 e68a5dc537d626622a9af6c9c7ddf665 over the normalised payload (ENV/ARG/CGCENV lines, minus CGCENV LOG and any .log lines). AFTER all three fixes: e68a5dc537d626622a9af6c9c7ddf665, byte-identical. This is the claim that the production launch environment did not change, and it is what makes 'no re-baseline needed' checkable rather than asserted.
- [artifact scripts/run_server.sh:1381-1401] The control-flow defect, fixed and re-measured. Before: LOOP_GUARD pushed for {default, L0=48} and DROPPED for {L1=48, L0=48+L1=48, L1=48+CGC_LOOP_GUARD=1}. After moving the guard block out of the L1 else-branch: pushed for {default, L0=48, L1=48, L0=48 L1=48} and correctly NOT pushed for L1=48+CGC_LOOP_GUARD=0, i.e. the opt-out is now the reason it is off instead of an accident. bash -n passes on both edited scripts.
- [artifact Backup/m123_oracle_gate/summary_skip0valued_siblings.json] Numerics confirmation: the gate's default arm against the v4 reference, on the rebuilt binary (libllama.0.0.239.dylib 952ed137 -> 6f856e31), is M1 9/9, M2 9/9, M3 9/9, full_fnv1a64 9/9, cross-tab {9,0,0,0}. The fingerprint predicted this and the gate confirms it; both were run because the fingerprint covers the launch environment and not the code path.

ALREADY RULED OUT (do not re-walk these):
- claim: Convert only the two flagged knobs and leave CGC_DBUF2 / CGC_FAST_WAIT alone, since nothing writes them.
  why false: It leaves two spellings of 'is this flag on' in the same header, which is the condition that produced the defect. The two extra conversions are behaviour-preserving by measurement today and cost one line each; leaving them means the next person who writes CGC_DBUF2=0 re-derives the same six-day failure.
- claim: Treat the LOOP_GUARD block as correctly guarded by an off-by-default, and tell users to pass CGC_LOOP_GUARD=1 when they want it.
  why false: Measured: CGC_SOFT_POOL_L1=48 CGC_LOOP_GUARD=1 still produces no CGC_LOOP_GUARD in the env, because the emission and the request sit in mutually exclusive branches. The knob is unreachable, not defaulted off, so that advice would have been a silent no-op.
- claim: Skip the re-baseline because 'nothing important changed'.
  why false: The reason is not that nothing changed -- the LOOP_GUARD fix is a real behaviour change for any configuration that sets CGC_SOFT_POOL_L1. The reason is narrower and checkable: the DEFAULT launch env is byte-identical (fingerprint e68a5dc5...), so no profile the gate measures can move. Stating the weaker, verified reason is what keeps the conclusion honest.
- claim: Quote a raw md5 of the CGC_DUMP_ENV output as the launch-env fingerprint.
  why false: Two runs of one profile differ (timestamped log path, free=NN%), while two runs of a different profile happened to agree -- so the raw hash is wrong in both directions. Only the payload normalised to ENV/ARG/CGCENV minus the LOG line is stable.

Landed: four header predicates routed through cgc_env_on() with per-knob notes; the missing `fi` and a corrected comment in run_server.sh; a value-semantics note in run_p1_mmap_stream.sh; rebuilt incrementally (libllama.0.0.239.dylib 952ed137 -> 6f856e31); launch-env fingerprint identical before/after for prefill250 (e68a5dc537d626622a9af6c9c7ddf665); the LOOP_GUARD table flipped from {default:yes, L0:yes, L1:no, L0+L1:no} to {yes,yes,yes,yes} with the opt-out respected; gate default arm 9/9/9/9 vs v4; CONVENTIONS A11; lesson eng-mh-0013 + eng-gate-0013 and this decision; guide docs/PRECOMMIT_HOOK_GUIDE_20260916.html. Next in leverage order: the hook-install path gap in check_build_tracked.sh:98 (`--absolute-git-dir` vs `--git-path hooks/`), which makes --install-hook print success while git never runs the hook in any linked worktree -- documented and demonstrated in the guide, not fixed; and the same non-empty spelling elsewhere in the tree, since this scan only covered llama-expert-cache.h for that family.

以下是一條引擎調校迴圈裡「付過代價」的觀測。請把它一般化成**一條可重用的規訓**——
換一個問題也適用，而且讀者手上沒有這筆 episode 也必須能照著做。

觀測（because）：
`ensure_batch` 的 `batch_owned` 註解自稱「hit slots + assigned miss slots」，但它是和 miss 指派**同一個迴圈**增量填入的。當池填滿時（identity prepopulate 填滿池且每個 `slot_last_use` 都是 0），`pick_slot` 的 LRU 犧牲者就是「最低且未被跳過」那一格；而淘汰會清掉被犧牲者的 slot 表條目（`llama-expert-cache.cpp:~555`，`slot_table[layer*n_expert + evicted] = -1`）⇒ 一次 miss 會把**後面還沒走到的成員**變成 miss。結果：`ids=[0..7]` 配上**一個**冷 expert，整批 8/8 全 miss，且整層映射整體位移 +1（`st[e] = e+1`）。單元測試上 HEAD 是 `st[0]=1 … st[15]=16`、0 hit/16 miss；兩趟之後是 `st[0]=16, st[1..15]=1..15`、15 hit/1 miss。修法除了拆兩趟，還要處理「一個 expert 已經擁有 slot 但 slot 表尚未發布」（`slot_owner[s]=e` 且 `slot_queued/loading` 已設而 `slot_table[e]` 未發布時，舊的 hit 判定只看 `slot_table[e]` ⇒ 判成冷的 ⇒ 給它第二個 slot）。

它實際被違反的紀錄（counterexample_observed）：
「這個集合不可能漏」的說法要小心：本輪之前曾把 09-14 日誌的 `st[e]=e+1` 讀成「兩個 expert 共用一個 slot ⇒ NaN」，而那是**引文抄錯**（原文 `st[1]=2`，白皮書寫成 `st[1]=1`）。修好引文後三行逐格自洽（`remap[i] == st[ids[i]]`），真正的異常是整體位移，不是共用。⇒ 當一行「不可能」的指控成立時，先回頭核**引文是不是原文**（見 `eng-gate-0021`），再動機制。另外：`il=2` 的 NaN 是下游簽名不是因——位移讓每個 expert 讀到別人的權重，且把池的 residency 上緣推過最後一個可用 slot（池區 OOB 讀），那才是會產生 NaN 而不只是「算錯」的那一類。

它管轄的檔案：`src/llama.cpp/src/llama-expert-cache.cpp`, `scripts/check/expert_cache_ensure_batch_order.cpp`, `docs/M1_POOL_SPLIT_COST_2026-09-14.md`
當一個「受保護集合」是由**同一個迴圈**邊走邊建、而它正是用來防止該迴圈造成破壞時，這個保護必然有順序依賴：只有它**之前**走到的元素被保護。判準是「這個集合在迴圈結束後才等於它宣稱的集合嗎」；若是，就要拆成「先認領全部、再變更」兩趟。註解寫著 exact-set invariant 不構成實作。

以下是一條引擎調校迴圈裡「付過代價」的觀測。請把它一般化成**一條可重用的規訓**——
換一個問題也適用，而且讀者手上沒有這筆 episode 也必須能照著做。

觀測（because）：
A GGUF header parser reproduced the loader's pool-capacity formula as `per_slot = MAX over all layers`. The loader computes that MAX over TRUNK layers only (it skips the NextN/MTP layer explicitly, so the trunk's pool cannot depend on how the head happens to be stored) while still counting every layer in the denominator. On the shipped model the two agree, because its MTP layer is THINNER than the trunk's binding layer -- so the tool matched the engine on every check that had been run (107/143/179 verified against two engine runs). The moment a second model was tried whose MTP layer is q8_0 and thus thicker, the tool reported 15 slots where the engine computes 148. Nothing about the first model's numbers looked wrong, and the tool had already been quoted in a plan document.

它實際被違反的紀錄（counterexample_observed）：
2026-09-17: `scripts/check/gguf_pool_geometry.py` vs the engine on `Ornith-1.5-35B-...gguf`. Uncorrected formula: per_slot = blk.40 (q8_0) = 3,342,336 B -> clamp(2 GiB/(41*3,342,336),8,256) = 15. Engine, same 2 GiB budget: `n_slots=29` with `LAYER_CAPS per-layer caps: total 1416 slots (avg 34.5/layer, min 29/layer)`. Corrected (MAX over trunk only): per_slot = blk.0 = 1,769,472 B -> 29, and the census prediction matches the engine's line exactly at both 2 GiB (1416) and 4 GiB (2616, engine `n_slots=59`).

它管轄的檔案：`scripts/check/gguf_pool_geometry.py`

When a tool reimplements an engine's formula, validate it on at least two artifacts that differ in exactly the dimension the formula's conditionals touch -- and make the tool print which branch it took. A formula that is only ever checked against one artifact encodes that artifact's accident as if it were the rule. Concretely: any reimplementation must read the SAME discriminators the engine reads (here, the GGUF's own nextn count), not infer them from the artifact in hand, because the artifact in hand may happen to make the branch irrelevant.

以下是一條引擎調校迴圈裡「付過代價」的觀測。請把它一般化成**一條可重用的規訓**——
換一個問題也適用，而且讀者手上沒有這筆 episode 也必須能照著做。

觀測（because）：
Two halves, both measured on 2026-09-15. (1) The bisect at --n-predict 24 reported p25-gputime md5 dc055e63 while two runs 25 minutes earlier at --n-predict 40 both reported 3d8fa55f, and the llama binary had been rebuilt in between -- which made 'the new diagnostic probes changed the model output' the obvious reading and would have sent me off to bisect the probe code. decode_bench.py hashes the whole completion and stores predicted_n beside it as n_tokens_sample, so that difference is pure truncation. (2) The sharper half: rung 2 ran every arm at the SAME --n-predict 24 and the actual generated lengths still came out 24/24/12/22/7/6, so on the five rows whose digest differs from the anchor the difference is confounded twice over -- it cannot by itself separate 'the trajectory diverged' from 'the same prefix, stopped earlier'. What does separate them is sample = texts[0][:160]: the anchor begins with a <think> reasoning preamble and every affected arm differs from its very first character, which is a length-free claim. The practical form: 'build the node' is a sentence about the builder's intent; 'the node exists' requires a consumer, and a design that only satisfies the first cannot be measured at all -- so it must not be planned as the control for a hypothesis.
